current_activity: directing defence from Army Group B HQ
notes: Rommel's Army Group B (re-formed) covered Netherlands to Loire; reserves incl. 2nd, 21st and 116th Panzer Divisions. Army Group B released 21st Panzer Division to Seventh Army at 05:00 on 6 June. HQ at Chateau de La Roche-Guyon; Rommel was in Germany on 6 June and returned to the HQ about 22:00 that night.

current_activity: requesting 7th Army withdrawal toward the Seine
notes: After Epsom, Rommel on 29 June asked Hitler for permission for the 7th Army to start a fighting withdrawal toward the Seine; Hitler later demanded unyielding defence. (Rommel and Rundstedt had been summoned to see Hitler at Berchtesgaden around 28 June per CMH/Epsom; position shown is Army Group B HQ, not Rommel s location.)

current_activity: Rommel badly injured; Kluge, the OB West commander, takes over Army Group B as well
notes: Event date: Rommel was injured in a car accident on the afternoon of 17 July when an Allied plane strafed his car; that evening, when the news became known, Kluge assumed command of Army Group B in addition to OB West (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 8 p. 169). Wikipedia's Army Group B page gives Kluge as commander from 17 July. Event support: the event itself is stated in the cited text (see Event date); only the headquarters place is a representative point. Location support fallback: no source read gives the headquarters place for 17 July; the point is the Chateau de La Roche-Guyon, the headquarters of claims C0011 and C0202, used as a representative point. Review (German Batch 1b, 27 October 2026): put into conflict group G021 with the new row C0767: the Schramm OKW war diary chronology (p. 458) has Kluge leading Army Group B "ab 19. 7.", two days after the 17 July of this row; this row stays preferred (two sources, the CMH and Wikipedia, against one) without a source that settles the difference; no value of this row changed.

Kluge übernimmt" and, a line further, "ab 19. 7. die Führung der Heeresgruppe B" (the OCR gives the words before "Gen.-Feldmarschalls" as "117: 125:", so the word "Verunglückung" is not in the text read; the accident is dated 17 July in the narrative of p. 325); the narrative (p. 325-326) dates the accident 17 July and says OB West "übernahm darauf zusätzlich die Führung der Heeresgruppe B" without a day. current_activity: Model takes over Army Group B (and OB West) from Kluge
notes: Event date: Wikipedia's Army Group B page lists Model as commander from 17 August 1944 (Hausser acting 15 to 17 August) and its OB West page lists Model as acting commander from 17 August. The CMH Green Book (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 532, 535, row of G018) puts the assumption of command at midnight after 18 August. The sources do not agree and neither is judged better, so both rows are disputed. Event support: the event itself is stated in the cited text (see Event date); only the headquarters place is a representative point. Location support fallback: the point is La Roche-Guyon, the headquarters of claims C0011 and C0202, used as a representative point. Review (German Batch 2 follow-up, 27 October 2026; notes and references only, no value changed): the Lexikon der Wehrmacht (Heeresgruppe B, "Generalfeldmarschall Walter Model 17. August 1944 - Kapitulation") and the Bundesarchiv listing RH 19-IX on the EHRI portal ("17.8.1944: Generalfeldmarschall Walter Model") also date Model's command of Army Group B from 17 August; they are one source family with the Tessin-based Wikipedia list, so the 17 August side of group G018 has one family and the CMH (midnight after 18 August, p. 535) the other. Schramm p. 465 and CMH p. 531 date his arrival at the headquarters to 17 August, a different event from taking over command (see C0933). The group stays disputed with no winner; confidence stays 0.3 because the place is a representative fallback point. Nothing in the dataset says that Model's command ended on 14 September: that date of the old task text is the move to Oosterbeek (see C0934); Army Group B was dissolved on 17 April 1945 (see C0937).

current_activity: Model arrives at the Army Group B headquarters at La Roche-Guyon to relieve Kluge
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary vol. IV, half-volume 1, p. 465 (OCR text): "Am 17. 8. traf" ... "Model im HQu der Heeresgruppe B in La Roche ein" (the OCR garbles "Gen.-Feldmarschall" between the two parts); CMH Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 530-531: "Model arrived on the 17th with instructions from Hitler to relieve Kluge and become OB WEST and Army Group B commander as soon as he was familiar with the situation"; German Wikipedia, Walter Model: "Am 17. August 1944 erhielt er die Brillanten zum Ritterkreuz und traf noch am selben Tag an der Westfront ein". Event definition: the arrival of Model at the army group headquarters on 17 August; this is not the date on which he took over command, which is disputed in group G018 (C0716: 17 August, Lexikon, Bundesarchiv listing and Wikipedia; C0715: midnight after 18 August, CMH p. 535), so this row does not decide that question; CMH p. 531 itself says he was to relieve Kluge "as soon as he was familiar with the situation". Event support: the war diary and the CMH both give the day (two families); the German Wikipedia repeats it. Location: La Roche-Guyon (PL0298), with a precision of 3 km. Context: Kluge, who had held Army Group B since July (C0714), left for Germany; Wikipedia lists Hausser as acting commander from 15 to 17 August (see C0716).

current_activity: Model takes over OB West and Army Group B; Kluge leaves for Germany
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 532 calls Model the commander-designate of OB West and Army Group B when he drove to the Fifth Panzer Army command post near Lisieux at 0600 on 18 August; p. 535 says that 'Model at midnight, after a day of inspection and conference in the west, assumed command'. The row reads that midnight as the end of 18 August, the date entered here (the text does not give the date; inferred from the two passages). Review (inferred value): the date 19 August is inferred; Wikipedia gives 17 August (G018 alternate). The sources do not agree and neither is judged better, so both rows are disputed. Event support: the event itself is stated in the cited text (see Event date); only the headquarters place is a representative point. Location support fallback: no source read gives the headquarters place for 18 or 19 August; the point is La Roche-Guyon, the headquarters of claims C0011 and C0202, used as a representative point. Review (German Batch 2 follow-up, 27 October 2026; note only, no value changed): CMH p. 531 shows that Model arrived on 17 August (new row C0933) but p. 532 still calls him the "commander-designate" at 0600 on 18 August; the arrival and the takeover of command are different events, and group G018 keeps both dates as disputed.

current_activity: Model moves the Army Group B headquarters to Oosterbeek near Arnhem
notes: Event date: battle-of-arnhem.com, "Field Marshal Walter Model flees head over heels from Oosterbeek" (read through the Internet Archive copy): "On September 14, 1944, Model moved his headquarters to Oosterbeek, more than 100 kilometers behind the front"; the page also says "He himself had moved into Hotel de Tafelberg on the Pieterbergseweg in Oosterbeek. His staff had moved into the nearby Hotel Hartenstein.". Event definition: the move of the headquarters to Oosterbeek on 14 September; CMH Siegfried Line ch. 7 p. 140 (C0825) puts the headquarters "in a hotel at Oosterbeek" on 17 September and does not date the move, so the two rows together give Oosterbeek from 14 to 17 September; English Wikipedia, Walter Model, says only that Model "established his headquarters at Oosterbeek" without a day. Event support: one web article for the day of the move; the CMH has the same place on 17 September (two families for the place, one for the day). Location: Oosterbeek, Gelderland (PL0545), with a precision of 3 km. Location support: the town is named by the article and by CMH; the two hotels are named only by the article, and no coordinate is given for them. Commander: Generalfeldmarschall Walter Model. Context: the CMH places the staff move one stage later, after the landing, at the II SS Panzer Corps headquarters beyond the IJssel (C0825).

current_activity: Model's Army Group B headquarters is in a hotel at Oosterbeek when the British airborne landing begins
notes: Event date: CMH Siegfried Line Campaign ch. 7 p. 140: "Model's headquarters of Army Group B was in a hotel at Oosterbeek on the western outskirts of Arnhem"; p. 141: "Model and his coterie folded their tents and stole away". Event definition: the headquarters at Oosterbeek on the day of the landing, 17 September; the evening move is described on p. 141 as to the II SS Panzer Corps headquarters beyond the IJssel, about eighteen miles east of Arnhem, with no named place. Location: Oosterbeek, Gelderland, with a precision of 3 km (the hotel is not named by the source). Location support: the town is named by CMH. Commander: Generalfeldmarschall Walter Model. Context: This corrects nothing in earlier rows. Model was Army Group B commander throughout September; he gave up only the OB West half to Rundstedt (5 September).

current_activity: Model dissolves Army Group B by order, effective 17 April; farewell to the staff reported at Haan
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 16 p. 369: "He at last decided, in effect, simply to dissolve Army Group B by order", "Model decreed on 15 April" and "As of two days later, 17 April"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, Heeresgruppe B: "Die Heeresgruppe kapitulierte am 17. April 1945 im Ruhrkessel"; Bundesarchiv RH 19-IX (EHRI): "Vernichtet durch Kapitulation im Ruhrkessel am 17. 4. 1945"; HistoryNet: "On April 17, Model decided to dissolve Army Group B; his men could find their way home. The order was ex post facto: Army Group B had already dissolved"; English Wikipedia, Army Group B: commander list "Walter Model (17 August 1944 – 17 April 1945)". Event definition: the end of Army Group B as a command: the order of 15 April took effect on 17 April, so the row carries the disestablished flag (dissolved by order); the destroyed flag stays false because the sources call it a dissolution or capitulation, not destruction in combat; the English Wikipedia text differs on the surrender ("the final section surrendered to the Allies on 21 April 1945") but its own list ends the command on 17 April; Model himself lived until 21 April (CMH p. 372: "During the afternoon of 21 April, Model asked his aide to accompany him and walked deeper into the forest", where he shot himself) and that death is a person event, so no row records it. Event support: the date 17 April is given by the CMH, by the Lexikon, the Bundesarchiv listing and Wikipedia (one Tessin-lineage family) and by HistoryNet (three families). Location: Haan (new place), with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: a town point for the Stadtwald of Haan; secondary single-source place. Location support: Konfliktlandschaften: "So habe er laut des bekannten Narrativs am 17. April 1945 im Stadtwald von Haan, südwestlich von Wuppertal, eine Art Abschiedsansprache vor dem Stab seiner Heeresgruppe B gehalten". Location caveat: the page itself calls this "das bekannte Narrativ" and has a transcript made from notes later; HistoryNet has the headquarters at Wuppertal (%s, 15 April)C0936; the place of Model's death is not certain: "Der exakte Todesort Models ist bis heute nicht mit Sicherheit bekannt".
